newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down in active trading on Tuesday on weak sentiment, with most contracts closing below 20,000 yuan, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 19,730 yuan ($2,377) per tonne, losing 460 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,020 and hit a low of 19,710.
The December contract 1996 fell 250 to 20,150, January 430 to 19,880, February 480 to 19,740, April 480 to 19,710, May 440 to 19,760 and June 360 to 19,850.
Combined volume rose to 107,720 tonnes from 70,190.
Copper opened low but near its intra-day highs, then heavy selling depressed prices, pushing most contracts to end at or near their intra-day lows, traders said.
Traders said weak market sentiment caused a large volume of stop-loss orders, pushing contracts sharply down.
"Heavy stop-loss selling emerged when copper breached the key 20,000-yuan support level," one trader said.
"Expectations of a rise in LME stockpiles made few players dare to build fresh long positions," he added.
Traders said many investors believe a new downward trend will start after sharp gains over the past few weeks.
"Not only poor fundamentals but also technical charts indicate that copper will fall further in the next few days," a second trader said.
Unless copper can recover the key 20,000-yuan level in the next few days, it will soon establish a mid-term downtrend, industry analysts said.
Aluminium ended down. December fell 100 to 13,700, January 100 to 13,850 and February 60 to 14,000.
Combined volume rose to 420 tonnes from 110.
